ac:layout-cell.h1: Invoice Sending API Reference and Spain Changes
ac:layout-cell.p: Sequence and Reuse Assessment · Solution Summary · Logical Feature Specification · Feature landing page

This API view owns field-level detail, request/response examples and contract issues. The Spain request proposal carries sender and recipient NIFs in the existing address type/value pairs, with separate platform selection. Explicit sender selection replaces the earlier null/default proposal. Recipient-platform omission depends on qualified resolution. Functional rules remain in SPEC-SEI-023; sequences and reuse checks remain in SPEC-SEI-024. Spain values and the proposed recipient-platform field need API-owner review.

The SPEC-SEI-022 combined overview shows Send, Correct and Cancel. These are ERP journey choices under SPEC-SEI-023 entry actions; they do not define a new request field or three API endpoints. Send and a new rectifying invoice use the invoice POST/upload flow. Cancellation addresses the existing resource through its separately qualified contract; the status POST is not an established cancellation command.
SPEC-SEI-047 service mapping owns the cross-service SPFE SOAP-to-Sage API mapping. This page owns Sending request/response fields, examples and contract changes.

Reuse POST /datasets/{datasetId}/e-invoices for one invoice. SPEC-SEI-023 OUT-00/10 records the agreed ERP selection responsibility and proposed per-invoice information. Reuse sender and recipient address type/value pairs for NIFs and accessPointId for sender selection. Add a proposed recipient-platform property. SPEC-SEI-024 owns sequences and engineering qualification.

Grey — Existing behaviour, calls and fields. Blue — Proposed Spain change. Red — Open question, Assumption, Gap or Source conflict. Always read the text label beside each colour. This follows SPEC-SEI-039 §3 and SPEC-SEI-040 “How to read the examples”. Examples use the preserved France-oriented contract and proposed Spain values where explicitly labelled. Proposed values and response fields are not approved wire contracts or implementation evidence.

tr.td: sender, recipient, accessPointAddressType, accessPointAddress, accessPointId

Existing: INT-SND01 defines sender and recipient as network-routing addresses, separate from seller/buyer in invoice content. The snapshot describes recipient.accessPointAddress as a Buyer key in the sender ERP; this is a confirmed wording defect. NIF is a legal tax identifier, not automatically a routing address. Proposed: es.nif, aligned with SPEC-SEI-040. Open: NIF-as-routing-address equivalence and NIE handling. Do not replace France's fr.siren. Spain's sender-side accessPointId meaning is Proposed and needs API-owner qualification. SND-G02; OUT-R04/11; INT-SND01/02.
Submission's required values and correlation

Source conflict: INT-SND01 says the guide requires sender.accessPointAddressType, recipient.accessPointAddressType and eInvoiceTypeCode; the OpenAPI schema omits eInvoiceTypeCode from its required list. Existing: Retain returned resource identity and optional erpInvoiceId linkage; the ERP reference is not an idempotency guarantee. INT-SND01/02; SND-G04/07.
Self-billing and extra recipients

Existing guide: buyer-to-seller route, one recipient per submission. Open: Qualify material issuer, represented business, actual destination, public-copy responsibility and supported eInvoiceTypeCode; the guide does not resolve those Spain roles. Accountant distribution remains OUT-Q02. SND-G02/06.
AR_Invoice, AR_CreditNote, AP_CreditNote

Existing: Preserve FR codes and the guide's type 381 association. Open: Supplied public formats use UBL 2.5 InvoiceType, including rectification, not CreditNote. Confirm any public mapping; never infer it from the FR label. SPFE-S08 p. 8; SND-G03.
attachments[].mimetype / filename

Existing: Guide names ubl-2.1/xml and application/pdf, filename 1–128 and address values 1–50. Open: It supplies no Spain UBL 2.5 MIME value. Qualify selected schemas, file roles and limits without silently extending them. SND-G02/03/07.
FR UBL/PDF or Factur-X choice

Existing: Real France UBL can have an optional PDF; Factur-X needs one hybrid file. Demo's two-file requirement is local. Open: Public restrictions on embedded files are distinct from MIME transport of UBL business documents; do not forward a hybrid or auxiliary PDF by default. SPFE-S02 Articles 3.5/4.4; SPFE-S03 p. 11; SND-G03.
Public batch, identity and results

Existing source: Catalogue states 1–100 invoices and authority evaluated per invoice. Source conflict: preserve the disputed 5120-byte unit limit; do not silently use KB. Business 200/406/400 request codes are not HTTP codes. Example locator/response fields do not prove CSV mapping. SPFE-S03/S08/S06; SND-G02.
Existing DTS

Existing candidate: Preferred transformation implementation candidate under PRD-SEI-223 FR43–46 and SPEC-SEI-008. Gap: Prove Spain field coverage, profile/version coexistence, rule isolation, final-byte validation, semantic preservation and operational ownership. FR UBL 2.1 or Factur-X support alone cannot establish this. SND-G03.

ac:layout-cell.p: The four-value proposal in §1.2 reuses the existing address fields. As France uses accessPointAddressType: fr.siren with a SIREN in accessPointAddress, Spain proposes es.nif with the NIF in accessPointAddress. No separate NIF property is needed. Spain scheme validation, including NIE-format NIF and provider routing support, remains under SND-G02. INT-SND01/02.

tr.td: Tax identity
Seller NIF and buyer NIF or NIE identify the invoice parties for tax purposes. NIE is a NIF class for a foreign natural person, not a separate scheme. PRD-SEI-101, “Seller NIF vs Buyer NIF/NIE”.
Routing address
Identifies the network participant or destination. A NIF is a routing-address value only where the selected network contract defines a scheme such as es.nif.
Certificate or signature
Any certificate or signature required for the selected action is separate from tax identity, routing address and authenticated-caller identity. Possession alone does not establish authority.

ac:layout-cell.p: Apply SPEC-SEI-023 OUT-10 to the dataset's exact selected sender connection. Apply OUT-09 separately: its six lookup cases require a qualified source. Private delivery does not require an unsupported Sage recipient lookup. Public-recipient checks remain subject to qualification; the reviewed SPFE bundle does not establish a recipient-directory API. SPEC-SEI-023 REF-LOOKUP.

PRIVATE_READY and PROVEN_NONE retain their existing meanings; the public-route decision also considers whether the customer communicated a private address. The two addressing pages are user-supplied. Their content status is Content not preserved in this repository. Their reported wording does not replace final legal evidence. Product and Spain Compliance must resolve the source conflicts. Until then, OUT-09 holds if the route condition is unclear. USR-ADDR01/02; OUT-09.

tr.td: No explicit accessPointId or it is null

Proposed: Reject the Spain send request with a clear sender-selection error. The ERP must supply its selected sender platform; do not default it from NIF or configuration. This replaces the earlier Spain null/default proposal. France behaviour remains unchanged.
Explicit selection is valid, connected and eligible

Proposed Spain behaviour: Allow any of the sender's ready, permitted connections for this invoice, including a private platform different from the one used for another invoice. Require a qualified delivery path to the recipient platform. Bind the selected connection, destination and evidence to the plan under OUT-10.
Explicit selection is unknown, disconnected or ineligible
Proposed: Return a clear error to the ERP. Do not replace it with the configured point or another route.
No valid configured sender access point exists
Proposed: Return a clear configuration error; do not choose a public sender point or recipient route silently.
Several sender access points are configured
Proposed: The ERP offers all ready, permitted sending connections. Select exactly one per invoice; do not change saved onboarding configuration or fan out.

ac:layout-cell.p: The sender access point may be public or private. accessPointId selects one of the sender's ready, permitted connections for this invoice; a later invoice may select another connection. The public recipient route is the recipient's destination under Spain policy. These are separate choices. The onboarding snapshots document access-point and connection operations, but not per-invoice selection. SND-G02; INT-AP07.

The ERP selection responsibility is agreed in SPEC-SEI-023 OUT-00/10 and USR-SND01. The table maps its four business values to data.attributes, reusing existing address fields. Only the recipient-platform property is new in this mapping. Its name is provisional; Spain values, validation and recipient-platform identifiers remain with the API owner under SND-G02/07.

tr.td: Sender NIF
Existing sender.accessPointAddressType and sender.accessPointAddress

Propose type es.nif and the sender NIF as the address value. Match the represented sender and selected connection under the qualified Spain mapping. A known NIF alone does not establish authority or readiness.
Sender platform
accessPointId — existing field, clarified Spain meaning
Required and non-null in this proposal. Choose any ready, permitted sender connection for this invoice under §1.1. It is not connectionId.
Recipient NIF
Existing recipient.accessPointAddressType and recipient.accessPointAddress
Propose type es.nif and the recipient NIF as the address value. Check consistency with invoice roles; qualify self-billing separately. It does not establish the recipient platform.
Recipient platform
recipientPlatformId — new

Required unless the selected integration can resolve the destination under a qualified contract. The API owner must define its catalogue or identifier namespace, provider/environment mapping and supported interconnection. Do not assume it shares the sender access-point catalogue.

ac:layout-cell.p: The type identifies the address scheme; the value carries the NIF under that scheme. Qualify whether the selected integration needs additional destination information under SND-G02 rather than duplicating NIF in another property. Existing seller/buyer fields inside the invoice retain their meaning.

tr.td: ERP supplies recipient platform and sufficient routing information

Use that intended destination under OUT-09/10 only where the selected sender platform supports the delivery path. Do not require unsupported Sage lookup or infer recipient readiness from sender setup. Different platforms require qualified interconnection, not sender onboarding to the recipient platform.
Selected sender platform cannot reach the recipient platform, or path support is unknown
Hold dispatch and return the route limitation and next action to the ERP. Another connected sender platform must not replace the explicit selection automatically. OUT-09/10; SND-G02/09.
Recipient platform is omitted and resolution is qualified for the selected integration

Resolve before dispatch. Retain the source, time and resolved destination with the original request. Multiple, ineligible or unresolved destinations follow OUT-09; omission does not mean public delivery.
Recipient platform is omitted without qualified resolution
Return a clear missing-destination error to the ERP; hold dispatch. Do not guess from NIF, copy the sender platform, search all providers or select SPFE automatically.
Recipient platform is unknown/unsupported, or resolution conflicts with the supplied destination
Hold dispatch and identify the destination issue and next action. Do not silently replace the ERP selection. An unchanged replay must retain the original resolution/plan under SND-G04.

ac:layout-cell.p: The API owner must qualify field-specific error representation and any resource/result changes needed to expose resolution. This proposal does not define new HTTP codes, an error enum or a recipient-directory endpoint. Functional checks are OUT-A03/04/05/23; compatibility checks remain in SPEC-SEI-024 §5.
ac:layout-cell.h2: 2 Proposed Spain extension of the Send e-invoice API
ac:layout-cell.p: This section proposes how Sending could reuse the France API for Spain. Existing marks behaviour documented by the France contract or guide. Proposed marks intent that needs API and Spain qualification. Assumptions, open points and source conflicts remain unresolved. The snapshot describes the France contract. It does not prove deployment or Spain support. INT-SND01/02.

tr.td: No change
Existing. Keep its current purpose. Lifetime, input binding and safe replay remain SND-G04.
No change
Existing. Preserve its current ERP-reference meaning; it is not an idempotency guarantee.
upload / returned uploadUrl
No change
Existing. Keep the current upload interaction and qualify completion/retry separately.
No change
Existing value: UBL. Proposed use: identify the structured invoice attachment. This does not establish its UBL version, profile, original/copy purpose or validity.
Status event
No change
Existing. Keep the event as processing evidence; it does not independently prove delivery or copy completion.
GET invoice detail
No change
Existing. Keep the detail read and current field meanings.
New value
Open. A Spain UBL 2.5 MIME value is not confirmed. Do not put an invented value in a request.
New value
Proposed: es.nif, aligned with SPEC-SEI-040 API-03. Open: confirm when NIF is a routing-address value and how NIE is handled.
New value
Proposed: es.nif, aligned with SPEC-SEI-040 API-03. Open: confirm when NIF is a routing-address value and how NIE is handled.
Changed meaning / validation
Proposed Spain-only change: explicit, non-null sender selection under §1.1. Remove the earlier null/default proposal. France remains unchanged.
New field
Proposed: recipient destination platform under §1.2. Omission requires qualified resolution; identifier namespace and final property name remain open.
New value
Open: Spain document mapping is not confirmed.
Recipient delivery and SPFE-copy results using history[] / statusAttributes
New field, if needed
Proposed: reuse existing history/status structures where meanings stay intact; add a per-action result shape only if needed. Open: the wire contract remains under SND-G05.
Cancel e-invoice
Proposed action; contract pending

Proposed API action: a distinct issuer action on the existing e-invoice resource under FP-SEI-002, subject to Architecture decision. Sending owns the request, response and recovery; Lifecycle owns the evidenced cancelled state. Invoice cancellation is separate from an Article 10 report or cancellation of an earlier report. Open: endpoint, payload, fields and wire result remain unselected. The existing status POST has no qualified invoice-cancellation binding. SD-CANCEL01.
Correct invoice — rectifying invoice
Proposed reuse of sending; Spain document mapping pending

Prepare and issue a new, separately numbered invoice under SPEC-SEI-015 IC-12. Submit it with the existing invoice POST/upload flow; the public mapping uses SendInvoice. Preserve the original reference and the new invoice's separate identity and lifecycle. Cancellation is neither a prerequisite nor a consequence. Open: qualify Spain invoice type, UBL mapping, DTS build and results under SND-G03/05/07. No new correction endpoint or CorrectInvoice SOAP service is selected. SD-CANCEL01.

ac:layout-cell.p: Engineering conclusion: Reuse the send call and existing address fields with proposed Spain values, explicit sender selection and a new recipient-platform field. Withdrawal follows the separate action direction above; its API contract is pending. SPFE, SERES, EDICOM, ZeroComa and B2Brouter are platform names, not values of accessPointAddressType; platform ID mappings require qualification.

Use SPEC-SEI-023 cancellation eligibility, including full customer rejection with the required reason, and SPEC-SEI-024 §2.4 for original/copy targeting, correlation and recovery. SPEC-SEI-022 combined overview shows the entry paths; SPEC-SEI-047 mapping owns their cross-service API/SPFE assessment. No cancellation request/response example is defined before the Architecture contract decision.

tr.td: POST /datasets/{datasetId}/e-invoices, returned resource ID and attachment upload URLs
Reuse the one-invoice resource and upload pattern. The POST accepts prepared files; preparation and ERP issuance remain outside this contract. INT-SND02; SND-G01.
PUT {uploadUrl}, status event, detail read, currentStatus, history[] and statusAttributes

Reuse as the observation baseline. Confirm event authentication, history correlation, freshness and Spain support. A processing status is not a recipient or public-copy result. INT-SND01/02; INT-ERR01; SND-G05.
Spain document and routing values
Proposed / Open

Propose es.nif for sender and recipient address types. Spain UBL 2.5 MIME and document mapping, routing-address equivalence and NIE handling remain open. Do not copy France enum values into Spain. SND-G02/03.
Per-invoice identities and platform selection

Reuse existing address type/value pairs for the NIFs and accessPointId for explicit sender selection. Add the §1.2 recipient-platform property. The snapshot calls accessPointId a “route destination”; qualify its Spain meaning and conditional recipient resolution. Sender-connection reads do not reveal the recipient platform. France remains unchanged. SND-G02/07.
Separate delivery and SPFE action results
Proposed / Open

Keep the existing status/history model where possible, with an additive per-action representation only if needed to make both outcomes independently observable. The example below is illustrative, not a wire contract. Private-platform copy-result/error reporting and failed-copy retry ownership are Gaps. SND-G05.
Sender connection availability and setup

SPEC-SEI-023 SND-G09 owns the setup boundary and evidence gates for the agreed selection model. Qualify simultaneous use of connections, address ownership and public readiness against the selected build. Per-invoice selection does not activate or reconfigure connections. Existing onboarding material is not proof of this capability.
Recipient lookup, route eligibility, customer configuration and access-point setup
Outside Sending
Owned by routing and onboarding. Sending consumes qualified sender configuration and recipient evidence; it does not create a national directory or connection.
UBL mapping, signing, SPFE transport and later lifecycle reports
Outside Sending
DTS, trust, public connector and lifecycle own their contracts. Sending coordinates the required handoffs and results.

ac:layout-cell.p: SPFE-S08 and the product specifications identify UBL 2.5 for the public route. The France snapshot lists ubl-2.1/xml and application/pdf. It does not establish Spain MIME, profile or provider support. No Spain MIME value is proposed. DTS remains the preferred transformation candidate, subject to qualification. SPFE-S08; SND-G03.

The transitional PDF goes to the recipient. Exclude it from every SPFE request, including attachments. Use a qualified private attachment path or a separate recipient channel. UBL 2.5 profile support and each provider's file rules remain open. RD238-T2; INT-SND02; SND-G08.

The supplied service-01 folder contains an invoice XML, SOAP request, business response and SOAP response. The invoice contains business data but no sender-platform or recipient-platform selector. The four-value proposal in §1.2 therefore still needs separate platform metadata. The following findings are example observations and proposed controls, not new externally mandated POST fields. REF-SND-EX01–03.

tr.td: Invoice/ID, IssueDate, supplier/customer PartyTaxScheme/CompanyID and PartyLegalEntity/CompanyID

After upload, check the request NIFs and document scenario against the actual invoice under the qualified role/identity mapping. Self-billing preserves seller/buyer positions. Retain the external issuer identity, invoice number and issue date separately from Sage resource ID and erpInvoiceId; do not add a duplicate legal-number/date input solely because these values occur in XML.
API, Validation; OUT-10/11; SND-G02/03. REF-SND-EX01; SPEC-SEI-015 invoice-type behaviour.
CopyIndicator=false in the supplied invoice

Bind original/copy purpose and exact representation to each planned SPFE action. The sample does not demonstrate faithful-copy generation. A required copy must use the qualified copy mapping; retain the issued original and any separate copy bytes. Do not add a global caller-controlled copy flag that can override the planned obligation. Whether purpose needs an API property or is derived remains open.
API, Spain Compliance, DTS; OUT-SPFE-R01; SND-G03/05/06. REF-SND-EX01; GLO-SEI-001 original and faithful-copy terms.
CustomizationID, ProfileID, InvoiceTypeCode=380; existing eInvoiceTypeCode

Qualify source/target syntax and profile versions, and the mapping between the Sage document code and actual XML type. The sample ProfileID omits ubl: from the final Annex I value recorded in SPEC-SEI-015 IC-SPFE-R02. It is not a passing fixture or a default to copy. The Invoice-2 namespace alone does not prove UBL 2.5. Hold unsupported or inconsistent content; do not silently repair uploaded issued bytes.
Format/Validation, DTS, API; SND-G02/03/07. REF-SND-EX01; SPEC-SEI-015 SPFE source contract binding.
Invoice lines, taxes, totals, payment terms, AdditionalItemProperty, AdditionalDocumentReference and Annotation

Keep business content in the XML and qualify its mapping/validation through existing DTS first. Do not repeat it as Sending JSON fields. A reference described as VERIFACTU does not establish a VERI*FACTU submission action. Its nested UUID is not evidence for a top-level invoice UUID field or the Spain composite-code encoding. The sample does not prove optionality or full country-field coverage.
DTS, Validation, Spain Compliance; SND-G03. REF-SND-EX01; SPEC-SEI-008 field-preservation controls.
attachments[].filetype, MIME part MimeType=application/xml and PartInfo/@href

Reuse filetype: UBL for the invoice file and qualify the Spain MIME/profile contract. The SOAP example's application/xml does not establish an accepted Sage attachments[].mimetype value. Validate actual uploaded bytes before dispatch and bind each action's file to the corresponding MIME Content-ID under the connector contract.
API, Integration; SND-G03. INT-SND02; REF-SND-EX02; SPFE-S16.
SOAP PartyInfo/From/PartyId, To/PartyId, MessageId, ConversationId and response RefToMessageId

Keep authenticated transport identity and message correlation separate from invoice parties and platform selection. The request comments identify From as the certificate sender's NIF and To as AEAT's NIF. To is not the invoice buyer or evidence of the buyer's platform. Resolve transport values from qualified connection/credential context; no additional ERP-supplied SOAP identifiers are proposed.
Public Integration, Identity; SND-G02/04. REF-SND-EX02; SPEC-SEI-011 PCN-SPFE-R02.
Business response ResponseCode, DocumentStatusCode, DocumentStatus/ID and ReferencedDocumentInternalAddress

Qualify how invoice detail/action results expose the source receipt, invoice correlation, raw result and locator. These are response/evidence concerns. Business 200 is not an HTTP status or proof of buyer acceptance; response ID and locator are not interchangeable with Sage invoice ID or CSV. Reuse the connector's result interpretation.
API, Integration; SND-G05. REF-SND-EX03; SPEC-SEI-011 PCN-SPFE-R03.

ac:layout-cell.p: Evidence limit: comparison on 18 November 2026 found both SOAP envelopes byte-identical to registered SPFE-S04/S07. The invoice differs from SPFE-S05: it removes AdditionalDocumentReference/DocumentTypeCode and changes the two PartyLegalEntity/CompanyID values. The response differs from SPFE-S06 by adding DocumentStatus/IssueDate. These local examples are not registered replacements; publication version and business-schema conformance remain unverified. The registered SPFE-S04–S08 paths are still missing. The reviewed WSDL baseline remains 29 October 2026. Integration/AEAT liaison must reconcile the evidence before using these examples as release fixtures. REF-SND-EX01–03; RES-SEI-002 release review.

Reuse currentStatus, history[] and statusAttributes for their existing processing meanings. The snapshot defines IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED and ERROR for operationStatus. ERROR is final for one attempt. These fields do not identify recipient delivery or the required SPFE action. Do not map France processing codes to Spain business statuses. INT-SND02; INT-ERR01.

Proposed: If the current resource cannot show both outcomes independently, add an action-result concept to the response and notification pattern. Each result identifies its purpose, outcome, reason when present and next owner. Keep an action unresolved until evidence confirms its result. Do not show full completion while a required action remains unresolved. The API owner must qualify this proposal under SND-G05.

This annotated request fragment illustrates the explicit-destination path on POST /datasets/{datasetId}/e-invoices. The existing address pairs carry the sender and recipient NIFs; es.nif is a proposed Spain value. Blue labels mark proposed values, fields or meanings; recipientPlatformId is a provisional name. Bracketed values are placeholders, not approved identifiers or MIME values. For qualified resolution, omit only recipientPlatformId; retain both address pairs, the sender selection and other required input. INT-SND02; SND-G02.

    }

ac:layout-cell.p: This response fragment is Proposed. It is not the current OpenAPI schema. proposedActionResults and its labels are unapproved placeholders. Recipient delivery may be complete while the required SPFE action is unresolved. Overall completion remains pending until both results are known. Support takes ownership only if platform recovery cannot resolve the outcome. SND-G05.
The fragment omits history entries, meta and an aggregate completion field for brevity. It does not define an aggregate field.

ac:structured-macro.ac:plain-text-body:
{
  "data": {
    "type": "e-Invoice" Existing,
    "id": "85f5d2c4-0ea3-4fca-9b71-12b507f4c201" Existing,
    "attributes": {
      "currentStatus": null Existing,
      "proposedActionResults": [ Proposed
        {"purpose": "recipient delivery" Proposed, "outcome": "completed" Proposed},
        {
          "purpose": "required SPFE action" Proposed,
          "outcome": "unresolved" Proposed,
          "errorReason": "external result awaiting reconciliation" Proposed,
          "nextOwner": "platform recovery" Proposed
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

ac:layout-cell.p: Reuse the France notification and detail pattern after API qualification. The ERP result must identify the action, reason and next owner. Separate transport errors, Sending errors, content errors and business lifecycle results. Return content errors to the ERP for correction. A correction creates a governed invoice revision. Retry eligible technical work only after reconciling the original result. Preserve completed actions. A failed invoice need not block later invoices. Sending cannot detect invoices the ERP never submitted without a separate capability. Keep accepted work visible and recoverable. SND-G04/05/07; OUT-A23/24.

tr.td: A. Public platform only
Proposed: Use the eligible public recipient route. No separate faithful copy is added after public issuance/interconnection.
Public eligibility and the six-case Spain recipient rule remain under OUT-09/SND-G02.
B. Private delivery plus required SPFE action

Proposed: Plan private recipient delivery and the required SPFE action as separate results. In Phase 2, the selected private platform sends the copy; this capability is an Assumption, expected but unconfirmed. The user-supplied PPIFE_competitor_analysis.xlsx marks SPFE integration as pending and is not preserved in this repository.

Prove the boundary between issuance and copy, action correlation and partial/lost-result recovery. How the private platform reports copy results/errors to Sage and who retries a failed copy are Gaps under SND-G05.
C. Several configured private providers

Proposed: Select any one ready, permitted sender connection per invoice through accessPointId. Different invoices may use different private platforms. The recipient platform may differ from the selected sender platform when interconnection is qualified. Never fan out or change saved onboarding configuration.
Qualify each sender connection and sender-to-recipient path under SND-G02/09. A ready connection does not establish reachability to every destination.
D. Sage operates as a private platform
Proposed: When Sage operates as the private platform, Sage sends the required SPFE copy. Keep the sender-platform role and delivery/copy results separate.
Provider-facing APIs and operator service remain outside this Sending proposal. Copy result/error reporting and failed-copy retry ownership remain open under SND-G05.

ac:layout-cell.p: These are issues in the preserved snapshot and guide, not verified runtime defects. API owners must decide corrections against the selected contract.

tr.td: SendInvoiceResponse.required; SendInvoiceResponse.properties
Gap: documents is required, but the schema defines attachments and no documents property.
Correct the schema/example inconsistency in the owning API contract; do not assume which name runtime uses.
SendInvoiceRequest.required and .accessPointId
Open: the field is required but its type allows null; the meaning of null is undefined.
Spain now proposes an explicit non-null sender selection under §1.1. Keep France unchanged; qualify country-specific validation and errors.
SendInvoiceRequest.sender and .recipient
Open: both parent properties are required, but neither nested object declares required child properties.
The schema does not enforce the address type/value required by the guide.
Proposed recipientPlatformId
Gap: this property and its conditional requiredness are absent from the preserved snapshot.

API owner must define its name, nesting, destination identifiers, supported resolution and error/result representation. NIFs reuse the existing address pairs; qualify Spain scheme validation separately. Do not send the proposed property to an unqualified build.
Open: the array schema has no minItems.
Empty attachment-list behaviour is not constrained by this schema.
traceparent and tracestate; INT-SND01 step 2
Source conflict: both headers have required: false in the OpenAPI snapshot, but INT-SND01 says they are required.
Keep the conflict open and confirm the selected contract. Do not describe them as required based on the snapshot.
SendInvoiceRequest.required and .eInvoiceTypeCode; INT-SND01
Source conflict: the schema omits eInvoiceTypeCode from the required list, while INT-SND01 says it is required.
Resolve the source conflict and confirm Spain document mapping separately.
SendInvoiceRequest.recipient.accessPointAddress; INT-SND01
Source conflict: snapshot description identifies a Buyer key in the sender ERP, while the guide defines sender and recipient values as network-routing addresses.
Correct the contract description; do not treat NIF or ERP buyer ID as the network address without a qualified mapping.

ac:layout-cell.p: Other relevant preserved onboarding contract issues are: GET /accesspoints declares datasetId as a path parameter although the path has no placeholder; connection requests allow address maxLength 114, while connection responses and Sending allow 50; string length constraints use maximum in some request properties; and the create example uses invalid IPv4 183.342.1.1. The postal-code example is numeric although the schema type is string; this confirms a type/example mismatch, not that 12345 is an invalid postal code.
